| Severity | **Moderate.** One non-overflowing bin and white plastic inside a planter are observed. No obvious pollution or overflow occurs, but clean-ground and no-retained-waste requirements are breached in a busy public station area, potentially affecting sanitation and appearance. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impact: plastic in the planter impairs public cleanliness despite not extending onto the ground. Possible short-term impacts: wind or trampling may disperse it and complicate cleaning; the prominent station entrance may attract complaints or negative publicity. |
| Potential causes | Possible causes include casual disposal into a pot or temporary placement when a bin was not found, insufficient or inconvenient bins, and inadequate inspections or cleaning. Artificial white plastic in S05-B-03 suggests human disposal; spare capacity at S05-B-02 indicates underused facilities. Review cleaning records, bin plans, inspections, and peak pedestrian–waste demand to verify causes. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, lower sanitation standards may encourage littering through a broken-windows effect; concealed planter accumulations may increase cleaning difficulty and costs; and distrust in urban management may impair the city's image. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** remove S05-B-03 plastic, inspect nearby pots and ground, and assess whether S05-B-02 requires more collection or relocation.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) add clearly labeled sorting bins and improve entrance layouts; (2) increase cleaning inspections, especially during peaks; (3) educate users; (4) inspect both planters and ground to prevent undesignated accumulations. |
| Priority | **Medium.** The problem breaches requirements and poses sanitation and appearance risks in a busy public station area, despite no severe pollution or overflow. Short-term action and stronger management are needed against spread or recurrence. |
